protocol: prereg step 4: 25 post-phrasing criteria pooled, provenance stripped, stable-sha256 order, FRESH independent Sonnet-class auditor sees only the blinded file; disputes adjudicated by a frontier (Opus) arbiter; 2 planted probe pairs per round

members.name: Ties a requested change to a specific paragraph of regulatory text
Mentions the number of members or constituents represented
Distinguishes what the rule requires from what it merely permits
Repeats the same sentence or phrase multiple times

final.name: Emotional-hook opening sentence before substantive content
final.audit_justification: Scores the rhetorical shape of the opening sentence (hook vs. direct substance), which the instruction explicitly frames as independent of the factual support that follows; a comment with an unhooked, substance-free opening scores 0 regardless of merit elsewhere.

final.name: Acknowledgment of tradeoffs and counterarguments
final.audit_justification: Requires the comment to actually identify and weigh a genuine tradeoff or counterargument, which is substantive engagement with competing considerations, not a surface feature.

final.name: Challenge to agency assumptions
final.audit_justification: A high score requires concrete evidence or reasoning aimed at a specific premise, dataset, or model in the proposal -- direct engagement with the agency's reasoning.

final.name: Reasoning-based persuasion vs rhetorical amplification
final.audit_justification: The top of the scale requires developed reasoning or evidence rather than rhetorical amplification, so a substance-free comment cannot score high; it does also register tone (measured vs. heated), which is a secondary style component.

final.name: Litigation-brief posture
final.audit_justification: The instruction explicitly says to 'score the posture itself, not whether the legal claims are correct' -- this is a shape/rhetorical-stance marker independent of substantive merit.

final.name: Identifies a conflict with operative statutory text
final.audit_justification: Requires quoting or precisely citing controlling text and showing the proposal cannot be squared with it -- substantive legal analysis and engagement with the agency's reasoning.

final.name: Docket-lineage familiarity
final.audit_justification: Measures whether the commenter narrates its own prior participation history in the docket, a submitter-identity/history fingerprint rather than an assessment of the substantive merit of the arguments made now.

final.name: Names a specific omission in the agency's supporting analysis
final.audit_justification: Requires locating a specific, named gap in the agency's supporting analysis and explaining why it bears on the decision -- substantive engagement with the agency's record.

final.name: Ties a requested change to a specific paragraph of regulatory text
final.audit_justification: The instruction explicitly directs the judge to 'score the anchoring, not the merit of the change requested' -- a bare, unsupported request naming a paragraph number can score high with no substantive reasoning behind it.

arbiter.model: Opus (frontier arbiter; criterion text + auditor verdict + proposer rationale)
arbiter.reason: Arbiter (Opus) upheld the auditor and OVERTURNED THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN PLANTED PROBE. This was authored as the SUBSTANTIVE member of probe pair P7; the phrasing pass sharpened 'Judge the anchoring of the request' into 'Score the anchoring, not the merit of the change requested', making the merit-disclaimer explicit. As written a one-line unsupported demand citing a paragraph number scores 10 while a data-rich comment naming only the topic scores 5, so the ordering tracks citation convention -- a professional-drafting fingerprint confounded with whether the commenter had counsel.

final.name: Tests whether the chosen instrument will actually bind
final.audit_justification: Requires substantive analysis of whether the regulatory instrument would actually change behavior (e.g., whether a threshold would ever bind), going beyond mere directional preference.

final.name: Traceable Evidence Use
final.audit_justification: Directly measures whether factual claims are supported by identifiable, checkable evidence and whether relevance/limitations are explained -- a core substantive-merit criterion.

final.name: Unintended-consequence safeguards
final.audit_justification: Requires pairing a plausible secondary harm with a concrete, actionable safeguard or mitigation -- substantive policy analysis, not a surface marker.

final.name: Unsolicited commendation of agency staff and process
final.audit_justification: Measures praise of agency staff/process beyond pro-forma courtesy; this is a tone/politeness marker unrelated to the substantive merit of the comment's regulatory content.

final.name: Formal institutional filing apparatus / letterhead conventions
final.audit_justification: The instruction explicitly states 'these are formatting conventions; score their presence only' -- a letterhead/apparatus density measure, not a substantive-merit measure.

final.name: Viable alternative design
final.audit_justification: Requires describing a practicable alternative regulatory design in enough detail that how it would work is clear -- substantive constructive engagement.

final.name: Organizational scale self-credentialing
final.audit_justification: The instruction explicitly says to 'score the presence and prominence of these claims, never whether they make the argument stronger' -- an organizational-scale self-credentialing/identity marker.

final.name: Distinguishes what the rule requires from what it merely permits
final.audit_justification: Requires correctly identifying mandatory vs. discretionary elements of the rule and reasoning about the distinction -- substantive regulatory-text analysis.

final.name: Repeats the same sentence or phrase multiple times
final.audit_justification: The instruction explicitly states 'score the repetition itself as a surface property of the text' -- a verbatim-repetition/formatting proxy unrelated to substantive content.

final.name: Operational Feasibility
final.audit_justification: Requires walking through concrete implementation steps and naming specific operational obstacles -- substantive feasibility analysis.

final.name: Traceable causal chain from the rule to the claimed effect
final.audit_justification: Requires a checkable, stepwise causal mechanism linking the rule to a claimed effect, making the claim falsifiable -- substantive reasoning quality.

final.name: Field observation that disconfirms a factual premise of the rule
final.audit_justification: Requires firsthand observation that contradicts a specific, named factual premise the agency relies on -- substantive first-hand evidence engaging the agency's reasoning.

final.name: Mentions the number of members or constituents represented
final.audit_justification: The instruction explicitly says to 'score only the presence of the stated constituency count, never whether it makes the argument stronger' -- a submitter-identity/scale marker.

final.name: Submission-production residue
final.audit_justification: The instruction explicitly states this is 'a surface property of the text; score the artifacts only' -- OCR/formatting/ingest residue, unrelated to substantive content.

final.name: Operational implementation microdetail
final.audit_justification: Requires specific, granular operational particulars (workflow, equipment, staffing, compliance process) drawn from inside an affected operation -- substantive operational engagement.

arbiter.model: Opus (frontier arbiter; criterion text + auditor verdict + proposer rationale)
arbiter.reason: Arbiter (Opus) upheld the auditor: a high score requires concrete in-operation particulars (workflow, equipment, filing, staffing, transition, compliance process) that must actually be present in the text; no surface tell or letterhead can manufacture it. It correlates with submitter type but does not score identity -- an insider letter with no particulars scores 0.

final.name: Specific, precise proposed regulatory fix
final.audit_justification: Requires exact replacement wording or a specific numeric threshold for the requested fix -- the specificity and actionability of the proposed substantive content itself, not merely its citation location.

B.upstream_parent: submitter resources, status, and perceived agency importance
